scenes.sub: A pointer that outlived the object it points to.
scenes.say: Dangling pointers. The address is still there. The object isn't.

scenes.head: Two pointers, one delete
scenes.say: p points to an int on the heap, and q is a copy of that address. Now delete p. The int is gone, but both pointers still hold its old address. Setting p to null p t r fixes p. But q still points to freed memory. That's a dangling pointer: it points to an object whose lifetime has ended. Writing star q is undefined behavior. The classic trap: nulling one pointer does nothing for its copies.

scenes.head: Other ways to dangle

notes.cue: as soon as that line ends

scenes.say: Delete isn't the only way. Returning the address of a local: x dies when the function returns. Compilers warn about this one. Pointers into a vector: push back may reallocate, moving every element, so first can be left pointing at freed memory. References and iterators dangle the same way. And a string view of a temporary string dangles as soon as that line ends.

lines: Dangling pointer: holds the address of an object whose lifetime has ended.
Causes: delete with copies around, returning locals, container reallocation.
Dereferencing it is UB. Fix ownership: smart pointers, values, sanitizers.
scenes.say: A dangling pointer holds the address of an object that's already dead. Common causes: delete while copies exist, returning locals, and container reallocation. Using it is undefined behavior. Fix the ownership with smart pointers and values, and catch the rest with address sanitizer.
